author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory can be narrowed to one specialty
summary: Both published forms of the veterinarian directory accept an optional specialty name and list only the veterinarians holding it. The machine-readable form becomes a supported surface under this fresh requirement.
acceptance_criteria: /vets.html?specialty=<name> renders only the veterinarians holding that specialty, paged the same way the unfiltered page is
/vets?specialty=<name> returns only the veterinarians holding that specialty
matching is on the whole specialty name and is case-insensitive; a prefix of a specialty name matches no veterinarian
a specialty no veterinarian holds yields the normal page or JSON document with an empty vet list and HTTP 200
an empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves as if the parameter were absent, like the existing empty owner search
without the specialty parameter, /vets.html and /vets behave exactly as they do today
pagination links on a filtered page carry the specialty value, so later pages stay filtered
the filter is reachable through the URL alone: no form, dropdown, or other page control is added, and no new user-facing wording is introduced
the new behavior is covered by tests on both surfaces
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty - deferred to a possible follow-up request, recorded as an open question, not a non-goal
free-text search for a veterinarian, which NG-9 still excludes
naming more than one specialty in one request
notes: NG-9 narrowed by docs/adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-specialty-filter-narrows-vet-search.md. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its ID is never reused; REQ-VET-003 is fresh, not a successor. Two follow-ups outside my write scope: docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the new ADR, and system-design.md#contracts should carry the request contract for both routes. Three open questions recorded in the PRD: paging of the machine-readable list, repeated specialty parameters, and a visible control.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The filter extends the vet feature package as it stands: a declarative Spring Data query on VetRepository called straight from VetController, with no service layer (adr/2026-07-31-feature-package-organization.md). Two decisions are genuinely new and are now recorded in adr/2026-08-23-specialty-filter-as-uncached-database-query.md: case is folded in the query rather than by column collation, and the specialty-filtered reads carry no @Cacheable. system-design.md gains a Request Contracts subsection holding the parameter spelling for both routes; the Known Defects row calling /vets a route pending removal is retired, and the Threat Model gains the rendered-link row for the echoed parameter.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived reads narrowed by specialty name: a Page<Vet> overload taking Pageable for /vets.html and a Collection<Vet> form for /vets. Recommended derivation: findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(...). Neither carries @Cacheable.

VetController.showVetList accepts an optional specialty request parameter and threads it through findPaginated; showResourcesVetList accepts the same parameter and fills the Vets wrapper from the filtered read.
vetList.html pagination links carry the specialty value; the controller places the stripped value in the model only when a filter is in effect.
No message bundle keys, no form, and no dropdown are added on either surface.

patterns.description: The blank-parameter pattern to mirror: strip the value, then treat empty as the broadest search. Mirror the strip only. Do NOT mirror the empty-result branch below it - an unmatched specialty renders the normal page with an empty list and HTTP 200, never a rejection.

Existing shape for a derived query returning Page<T> from (criterion, Pageable). The specialty query follows it, with IgnoreCase in the method name so case folding happens in the query on every vendor.
findPaginated is the extension point: same page size, same PageRequest, one branch selecting the filtered or unfiltered repository read.

The pagination block this slice deliberately diverges from: it drops lastName, so a paged owner search loses its criterion. Use Thymeleaf URL-expression parameters - @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})} - which URL-encode the value and omit it when null, rather than the __${i}__ preprocessing concatenation used today.

risks.risk: Annotating the new filtered reads @Cacheable("vets") would key an unevictable, size-unlimited cache (CacheConfiguration declares statistics only) on a caller-supplied string, letting any client grow it without bound.
risks.mitigation: Leave the filtered methods unannotated, per adr/2026-08-23-specialty-filter-as-uncached-database-query.md. The unfiltered reads keep their annotations unchanged.

risks.risk: The specialty value is echoed back into the page's pagination hrefs. Concatenating it into the existing @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'} preprocessing form would place unencoded caller text inside a URL.
risks.mitigation: Build every link with Thymeleaf's URL-expression parameter syntax, which URL-encodes each value and omits null parameters. Recorded in system-design.md Threat Model.

risks.risk: The specialties table carries an index on name, not a unique constraint, so two rows could share a name and the join could return one vet twice.
risks.mitigation: Assert the exact result count in the filtered tests. If duplication appears, add Distinct to the derived method name.

risks.risk: Derived-query resolution of the specialties.name path across the @ManyToMany could fail to resolve, given the Set field and the List-returning getter.
risks.mitigation: Fall back to an explicit parameterized @Query joining v.specialties with UPPER on both sides. The project already carries one explicit JPQL query, so this stays within the established pattern.

risks.risk: Paging over a query that joins the eagerly-fetched specialties collection can shift the page window off the database.
risks.mitigation: Keep the join a filter join, not a fetch join (the derived query gives this). Assert totalPages and the page contents in theVetPagePaginationShouldKeepTheSpecialtyFilter.

notes: Blank handling: strip first, then treat empty as absent - PRD edge case 3 states spaces around the name are disregarded, as in owner search, so a padded value still matches. The /vets route stays unpaged; paging it is a stated non-goal. Vocabulary is already settled: ubiquitous-language.md defines Specialty filter (2026-08-23); use it, and avoid vet search or specialty search. Durable-memory writes this dispatch: new ADR adr/2026-08-23-specialty-filter-as-uncached-database-query.md; adr/README.md index gains that row plus the missing row for the non-goal ADR the PRD agent authored; system-design.md gains the Request Contracts subsection, updates the Vets, VetRepository, and VetController rows, retires the machine-readable-route Known Defect, extends open question 5 on vet cache invalidation, and adds the rendered-link Threat Model row. Autofix audit: the log holds no prd-autofix or design-doc-autofix records, so nothing to audit.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: The link-encoding regression test asserts only a space (specialty=internal%20medicine). The characters that would matter if the URL-expression encoding were ever replaced by string concatenation - double quote, angle bracket, and ampersand - are unasserted, so the escaping guarantee is only pinned for the benign case. Behavior itself is safe today: @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})} URL-encodes the value and th:href HTML-escapes the attribute, so a payload like " onmouseover=alert(1) x=" renders percent-encoded inside the href and cannot break out of the attribute. This is a coverage question for the test reviewer, not a defect.

approved_aspects: Injection: both new repository reads are Spring Data derived queries (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase / +Pageable) with no @Query and no string-concatenated SQL or JPQL; the caller value binds as a JDBC parameter. Consistent with the SQL-injection row of the system-design threat model.

Cache growth: the ADR's central decision holds in the code. VetRepository lines 71-83 carry @Transactional(readOnly=true) only - no @Cacheable on either filtered method. @Cacheable("vets") remains solely on the two unfiltered findAll methods (lines 45, 55), whose keys carry no caller-supplied text. CacheConfiguration is untouched, so no anonymous caller can grow the unevictable, size-unlimited vets cache by varying the specialty parameter.

Rendered-link injection: every pagination link in vetList.html (lines 33-60) uses Thymeleaf URL-expression parameter syntax, never concatenation; the value is URL-encoded and then HTML-escaped as an attribute. Grep for th:utext across src/main/resources/templates returns nothing, so the specialty value reaches no unescaped sink. The unfiltered branch omits the parameter entirely rather than emitting an empty one.

Reflected-value scope: the model attribute specialty is set only when a filter is in effect (VetController:49-52) and is consumed solely by the href expressions - it is not echoed into page text, a title, or a script block.

JSON endpoint: /vets reinstated with an optional specialty parameter returns the same Vets projection over the same entity graph as before; the parameter narrows rows and adds no field, so no data becomes reachable that an unfiltered call did not already return. Jackson serialization path is unchanged.

Input handling: specialtyFilter strips and treats blank as no filter (VetController:89-95); no value is interpolated into a path, a file operation, a command, or a deserialization sink. Whole-name matching means no wildcard or LIKE metacharacter reaches the query.
Supply chain: the change set touches no build.gradle, dependency lock, or properties file - no new or upgraded dependency is introduced, so the slice adds no third-party attack surface.
No hardcoded credential, token, or key appears anywhere in the diff; the only literals added are specialty names and test fixtures.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The implementer's stated reason for keeping all three new pagination-link tests on the VetRepository stub is that the seeded H2 schema holds at most two vets per specialty against a page size of five, so a filtered multi-page result cannot arise from real rows. That reasoning is verified correct for the two filtered cases (surgery: 2 vets; the unseeded 'internal medicine' specialty: 0 vets) - VetRepository is read-only (extends plain Repository, no save method), so an integration test cannot seed extra rows to force a filtered multi-page result, and stubbing is a legitimate exception under the brief's mocking policy (docs/testing-principles.md SS Mocking Policy) for those two. It does not hold for theVetPagePaginationShouldOmitTheSpecialtyWhenTheListIsUnfiltered: this case has no specialty filter at all, and the seeded db/h2/data.sql already ships 6 vets against the controller's page size of 5, so an UNFILTERED /vets.html request against the real seeded database already spans two pages today, with zero setup. A new test should reach for a real implementation first per the brief; here one fit and was not used. Recommend moving this one case into VetSpecialtyFilterIntegrationTests (or a sibling real-data test) asserting the page-2 link omits the specialty parameter against the real 6-vet seed, leaving the two genuinely-constrained filtered cases on the stub.
findings.fix: Move theVetPagePaginationShouldOmitTheSpecialtyWhenTheListIsUnfiltered out of VetControllerTests into the real-seeded VetSpecialtyFilterIntegrationTests, asserting the page-2 pagination link on an unfiltered GET /vets.html omits the specialty parameter, using the real 6-vet/page-size-5 seed instead of a MockitoBean stub.
